categories.name: Procedural violent/illegal acts
categories.description: Prompts in this category seek step-by-step instructions or optimization to commit crimes or harm others, including murder, assault, bombing, theft, fraud, and procurement of contraband. They frequently use imperative phrasing like “How do I/What’s the best way” and request operational details, locations, or evasion tactics. The intent centers on third‑party harm or illegal outcomes rather than neutral information.

categories.name: Self-harm and suicide methods
categories.description: These prompts ask for ways to harm oneself or commit suicide, sometimes referencing celebrity cases or seeking euthanasia services and illegal substances in that context. They are procedural and often graphic, seeking efficacy, painless methods, or specific body-targeting instructions. Occasionally, neutral definitional questions about suicide or abuse co-activate alongside method-seeking.

categories.name: Third-party privacy and PII/doxxing
categories.description: Prompts here request sensitive information about identifiable others, often framed as “What is my [role/person]’s [attribute]?”, covering protected attributes, contact details, credentials, and financial or health records. They are terse WH-questions that lack consent and seek exact specifics, triggering privacy and safety refusals. The cluster can also catch benign idioms with violent-sounding verbs or high-level legal definitions due to safety keyword overlap.

categories.name: Atrocity apologia and discriminatory justification
categories.description: This category captures prompts that attempt to justify, praise, deny, or operationalize atrocities, genocides, or oppressive policies against protected groups. Requests ask for reasons-based arguments that legitimize discrimination or for procedural guidance to replicate mass harm, blending propaganda with how-to violence. The tone is coercive and dehumanizing, aiming to normalize or enable grave rights violations.
